sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars, and I am standing in the Galapagos in front of a congress of marine iguanas.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯，我正站在加拉帕戈斯群岛上，面对着一大群海鬣蜥。

sentences.en: They're piled on top of each other.
sentences.zh: 它们一只叠着一只地挤在一起。

sentences.en: Occasionally, if you can make it through the sound of the waves and the wind, you can hear them spitting out salt water from their nose.
sentences.zh: 偶尔，如果你能盖过海浪和风声，就能听到它们从鼻子里喷出盐水的声音。

sentences.en: They just sneeze on each other and lay on each other, and they seem like they enjoy life pretty well.
sentences.zh: 它们只是互相打喷嚏，叠趴在一起，看起来对生活相当满意。

sentences.en: Last week, I was in the Galapagos Islands, which for me is the ultimate travel destination.
sentences.zh: 上周，我在加拉帕戈斯群岛，对我来说，这是终极的旅游目的地。

sentences.en: I'm on Fernandina Island, where the marine iguanas are very plentiful.
sentences.zh: 我在费尔南迪纳岛，那里的海鬣蜥非常多。

sentences.en: Also the flightless cormorant, who keeps his wings open while he's just standing on a lava rock.
sentences.zh: 还有不飞鸬鹚，它站在熔岩上时，翅膀一直张开着。

sentences.en: My family hiked and swam with these astounding creatures in this completely foreign landscape.
sentences.zh: 我和家人在这个完全陌生的风景中，与这些神奇的生物一起徒步和游泳。

sentences.en: The iguanas just match the lava.
sentences.zh: 鬣蜥的颜色和熔岩完美融合。

sentences.en: You can almost step on them.
Since there are no predators, they have no fear of humans at all.
sentences.zh: 由于没有天敌，它们对人类毫无畏惧。

sentences.en: And you can just walk right up to them.
sentences.zh: 你可以径直走到它们跟前。

sentences.en: You don't touch them, but you can just walk real close to them and take a picture.
sentences.zh: 你不能碰它们，但你可以走到离它们非常近的地方拍照。

sentences.en: And sometimes they sneeze on you.
sentences.zh: 有时它们还会冲你打喷嚏。

sentences.en: I'll probably end up doing a story about it someday, despite myself, but fundamentally, I was there just to be there.
sentences.zh: 尽管我有些不情愿，但最终我可能会写一篇关于它的故事，不过本质上，我去那里只是为了感受当下。

sentences.en: For 40 years of my life, I could barely conceive of doing this kind of trip, but I have that privilege now.
sentences.zh: 在我生命的前40年里，我几乎无法想象自己会进行这种旅行，但我现在有了这种特权。

sentences.en: And after leaving the islands, my first thought was, I have to do this more often.
sentences.zh: 离开群岛后，我的第一个念头就是：我以后要多来几次。

sentences.en: Experiencing as much of the world as possible is something that I need to place a little closer to the foundation of my hierarchy of needs.
sentences.zh: 尽可能多地体验这个世界，是我需要在需求层次理论中放得更靠基础地位的事情。

sentences.en: This is something the team at Atlas Obscura figured out a long time ago.
sentences.zh: 这是“阿特拉斯奇观”团队很久以前就明白的道理。

sentences.en: Atlas Obscura is the definitive guide to the world's hidden wonders.
sentences.zh: “阿特拉斯奇观”是探索世界隐藏奇观的权威指南。

sentences.en: They write books, they host experiences, they lead excursions, and they have a podcast that I really enjoy.
sentences.zh: 他们写书、举办体验活动、带领远足，还有一个我非常喜欢的播客。

sentences.en: So in order for me to have enough time to take my life-changing trip,
sentences.zh: 因此，为了让我有足够的时间去进行这场改变人生的旅行，

sentences.en: we are presenting a couple of life-changing trips from Atlas Obscura that capture their adventurous and curious spirit.
sentences.zh: 我们挑选了几次来自“阿特拉斯奇观”的改变人生的旅行，它们捕捉到了那种冒险和好奇的精神。

sentences.en: This is the Beachy Island Graves.
Way, way up north, far in the Canadian Arctic, there's a lonely, windswept island.
sentences.zh: 在极北之地，加拿大北极地区的深处，有一个孤独、饱受风吹日晒的岛屿。

sentences.en: No trees, nothing, just pebble beach that backfire mountains.
sentences.zh: 没有树木，什么都没有，只有背靠群山的卵石海滩。

sentences.en: Even in summer, it can be well below freezing on this island.
sentences.zh: 即使在夏天，这座岛上的温度也可能远在冰点以下。

sentences.en: Sheets of ice float by in the bay, a crisp wind whips across its pebble beaches, and there are no signs of life.
sentences.zh: 浮冰在海湾中漂过，凛冽的狂风掠过卵石海滩，看不到任何生命的迹象。

sentences.en: Out here, standing alone on this rock, are four simple wooden headstones.
sentences.zh: 在这片荒凉中，孤零零地立在这块岩石上的，是四块简陋的木制墓碑。

sentences.en: These graves are the remnants of one of the most infamous Arctic expeditions of all time.
sentences.zh: 这些坟墓是北极历史上最声名狼藉的探险活动之一的遗迹。

sentences.en: I'm Dylan Thuris, and this is Atlas Obscura, an exploration of the world's strange, incredible, and wondrous places.
sentences.zh: 我是迪伦·图里斯，这里是“阿特拉斯奇观”，带你探索世界上奇特、不可思议和奇妙的地方。

sentences.en: In this two-part series, we are going to venture out towards those frozen graves, following two groups of adventurers, separated by more than 170 years.
sentences.zh: 在这个两部分组成的系列中，我们将冒险前往那些冰冷的坟墓，沿着两群相隔170多年探险者的足迹前行。

sentences.en: And we'll play witness to the disasters that befell them all.
sentences.zh: 我们将共同见证降临在他们所有人身上的灾难。

sentences.en: So I had a great time.
A description of heroism never more apt as when applied to those who braved the Arctic.
sentences.zh: 对英雄主义的描述，再也没有比用在那些勇闯北极的人身上更贴切的了。

sentences.en: I have to admit that I am a sucker for true life adventure stories.
sentences.zh: 我必须承认，我是一个真实探险故事的狂热爱好者。

sentences.en: The extraordinary tales, the human spirit against unforgiving odds, I kind of eat it up.
sentences.zh: 那些非凡的故事，人类在无情逆境中的精神，我简直百听不厌。

sentences.en: My bookshelf is embarrassingly full of these kinds of stories.
sentences.zh: 我的书架上尴尬地塞满了这类故事。

sentences.en: And included among them, of course, is one of the classics, one of the epics, the story of the Franklin Expedition.
sentences.zh: 其中当然少不了经典之作、史诗之作——富兰克林远征的故事。

sentences.en: Sir John Franklin was, at 59, a veteran of two overland expeditions in the North American Arctic.
sentences.zh: 约翰·富兰克林爵士在59岁时，已经是北美北极地区两次陆上探险的老兵了。

sentences.en: On the morning of May 19, 1845, Captain John Franklin said goodbye to his wife, Lady Jane Franklin, and stepped aboard his new ship.
sentences.zh: 1845年5月19日清晨，约翰·富兰克林船长向妻子简·富兰克林夫人告别，踏上了他的新船。

sentences.en: This was the beginning of his fourth Arctic mission.
sentences.zh: 这是他第四次北极任务的开始。

sentences.en: He already had a reputation for being tough.
His nickname in the press was the man who ate his boots.
sentences.zh: 媒体给他的绰号是“吃靴子的男人”。

sentences.en: Because during one of his previous Arctic expeditions, he and his crew had survived by eating lichen and their own boot leather.
sentences.zh: 因为在之前的一次北极探险中，他和船员靠吃地衣和自己的皮靴皮革才得以存活。

sentences.en: At nearly 60 years old, Franklin was embarking on one more mission, one that he knew would define him.
sentences.zh: 将近60岁的富兰克林即将开始又一次任务，他深知这将定义他的一生。

sentences.en: Franklin was attempting the Victorian era's version of the moonshot.
sentences.zh: 富兰克林正在尝试维多利亚时代版本的登月计划。

sentences.en: Franklin was going to try and chart the Northwest Passage.
sentences.zh: 富兰克林要尝试绘制西北航道的地图。

sentences.en: Finding the passage was all about money, about trade.
sentences.zh: 寻找这条航道全是为了金钱和贸易。

sentences.en: European countries had wanted a faster route to Asia so that they could do more exporting.
sentences.zh: 欧洲国家一直想要一条通往亚洲的更快路线，以便进行更多的出口贸易。

sentences.en: And the expeditions to find this trade route date back to 1497.
sentences.zh: 而寻找这条贸易路线的探险可以追溯到1497年。

sentences.en: The voyage meant sailing up and over North America through the incredible expanse of Arctic ice in order to ultimately reach the other side, the Pacific Ocean.
sentences.zh: 这次航行意味着要乘船向北穿过北美，越过广袤无垠的北极冰层，最终到达另一边的太平洋。

sentences.en: And even as the route lost its luster as an economic possibility, the British stayed obsessed with charting it.
sentences.zh: 即便这条航道作为经济通道的光芒已经褪去，英国人仍然对绘制它的地图痴迷不已。

sentences.en: By the time Franklin set sail in 1845, many had tried, failed, and died.
sentences.zh: 到富兰克林于1845年起航时，已经有许多人尝试过、失败过并丧生了。

sentences.en: The two ships on the expedition, the HMS Erebus and the HMS Terror, had been reinforced to withstand the ice.
sentences.zh: 远征的两艘船，幽冥号和惊恐号，都经过加固以抵御浮冰。

sentences.en: And they were being sailed by an experienced crew of 134 sailors and officers.
sentences.zh: 它们由134名经验丰富的海员和军官组成的船员队伍驾驶。

sentences.en: They even had a monkey on board named Jacko.
sentences.zh: 他们的船上甚至还有一只名叫杰科的猴子。

sentences.en: But most of all, they had lots and lots of food.
sentences.zh: 但最重要的是，他们带了大量大量的食物。

sentences.en: 36,000 pounds of biscuits, 32,000 pounds of salted beef, 8,000 tins of preserved meat.
They had 1,000 pounds of just mustard and 3,600 gallons of booze.
sentences.zh: 他们有1,000磅的纯芥末和3,600加仑的酒。

sentences.en: It was enough food to last every sailor for three years.
sentences.zh: 这些食物足够让每个水手吃上三年。

sentences.en: When did you decide to go to the Arctic?
sentences.zh: 你是什么时候决定去北极的？

sentences.en: What kind of incited you to want to take that trip?
sentences.zh: 是什么促使你想要进行那次旅行的？

sentences.en: You know, I have no idea.
Other than I like adventures, I was interested in the Franklin Expedition.
sentences.zh: 除了我喜欢冒险，我对富兰克林远征很感兴趣之外。

sentences.en: And in 2018, 173 years after the Franklin Expedition sailed, John Stewart of Thunder Bay, Canada, climbed onto a little Zodiac, kind of inflatable boat,
sentences.zh: 2018年，在富兰克林远征启航173年后，来自加拿大桑德贝的约翰·斯图尔特爬上了一艘小型橡皮艇——一种充气船，

sentences.en: and motored out to a large cruise ship floating in the Arctic Bay.
sentences.zh: 开着它驶向停泊在北极海湾的一艘大型游轮。

sentences.en: At 91 years old, John Stewart was almost certainly the oldest passenger on the expedition.
sentences.zh: 91岁的约翰·斯图尔特几乎可以说是这次远征中最年长的乘客。

sentences.en: Well, I, you know, I'm not one to go and sit on the beach down in Florida, and I like to follow history if I can.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，我不是那种去佛罗里达海滩坐着的人，如果可能的话，我喜欢追寻历史。

sentences.en: The ship John was boarding was called the Academic Ioffi, and it was part of an Arctic tourist cruise run by a company called One Oceans and sailed by an experienced Russian crew.
sentences.zh: 约翰登上的这艘船名叫“院士约费”号，它是“海洋之光”公司运营的北极旅游邮轮的一部分，由经验丰富的俄罗斯船员驾驶。

sentences.en: The purpose of the cruise was to follow in Franklin's footsteps, to bring Franklin-obsessed travelers one step closer to the object of their historical fascination.
sentences.zh: 这次巡航的目的是追随富兰克林的足迹，让痴迷于富兰克林的旅行者更接近他们历史迷恋的对象。

sentences.en: And the ship, the Ioffi, was carrying a total of 126 people, just about the size of Franklin's original crew.
sentences.zh: 约费号船上一共有126人，刚好和富兰克林最初的船员规模差不多。

sentences.en: Although, to be fair, the cruise expedition that John Stewart was on was a little bit cushier than Franklin's.
sentences.zh: 虽说句公道话，约翰·斯图尔特参加的这次邮轮远征比富兰克林的要舒适一些。

sentences.en: Meals were served via a buffet line, and there were optional yoga classes.
sentences.zh: 餐食是通过自助餐形式提供的，还有可选的瑜伽课程。

sentences.en: John had opted for the cheaper shared bunk option.
sentences.zh: 约翰选择了较便宜的共享铺位选项。

sentences.en: So, I shared a cabin with somebody I'd never met before, and I was shown to my cabin, and I was the only person there.
sentences.zh: 所以，我和一个从未见过面的人合住一个客舱，当我被带到房间时，里面只有我一个人。

sentences.en: But eventually, this young, good-looking, smart fellow stepped in, and I'm your bunkmate.
sentences.zh: 但最终，这个年轻、帅气、聪明的家伙走了进来，说：“我是你的舱友。”

sentences.en: I think we both hit it off pretty well.
Well, at a very short period of time, I think we became good friends.
sentences.zh: 嗯，在很短的一段时间内，我认为我们成了好朋友。

sentences.en: I was there as part of an Atlas Obscura trip, helping to make sure our travelers got what they needed.
sentences.zh: 我是作为“阿特拉斯奇观”行程的一部分去的，负责确保我们的旅行者得到他们需要的东西。

sentences.en: But John wasn't actually one of our Atlas Obscura travelers.
sentences.zh: 但约翰其实并不是我们的“阿特拉斯奇观”旅行者之一。

sentences.en: He was just my delightful, unexpected, 91-year-old bunkmate.
sentences.zh: 他只是我那可爱、意料之外的91岁舱友。

sentences.en: But that first night, John and I stayed up talking, and he told me all about his wife and their three sons.
sentences.zh: 但在第一天晚上，约翰和我熬夜聊天，他跟我聊起了他的妻子和三个儿子。

sentences.en: Matter of fact, when they were young, we did a lot of canoeing around here.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在他们年轻的时候，我们在这一带划过很多独木舟。
这里是划独木舟的绝佳去处。

sentences.en: But they were quite adventurous trips, and I really enjoyed them.
sentences.zh: 但那些都是相当具有冒险性的旅行，我真的很喜欢。

sentences.en: He told me all about his adventures, and about how he'd been traveling alone more since his wife passed away.
sentences.zh: 他跟我讲了他所有的冒险经历，以及自从妻子去世后他是如何更多地独自旅行的。

sentences.en: And even how just a short time before our trip, he'd actually lost one of his three sons in a biking accident.
sentences.zh: 甚至还讲到就在我们旅行前不久，他在一场自行车事故中失去了三个儿子中的一个。

sentences.en: It's a sad thing, but it's life.
sentences.zh: 这是一件令人伤感的事，但这就是生活。

sentences.en: You can't really go about it.
We had some wonderful times together, and almost every year we went on some major holiday somewhere.
sentences.zh: 我们曾有过美好的时光，几乎每年我们都会去某地度过一个盛大的假期。

sentences.en: That evening, I made a note to myself.
sentences.zh: 那天晚上，我记在心里一个小本本上。

sentences.en: John and I were going to stick together on this trip.
sentences.zh: 这次旅行中，我和约翰要形影不离。

sentences.en: He was the heartiest 91-year-old I had ever met.
sentences.zh: 他是我见过的精神最好的91岁老人。

sentences.en: But I figured we could both use a good crewmate.
sentences.zh: 但我想我们俩都需要一个好的船友。

sentences.en: On July 6, 1845, Captain John Franklin wrote home from the Whale Fish Islands, just off the coast of Greenland.
sentences.zh: 1845年7月6日，约翰·富兰克林船长从格陵兰岛海岸附近的鲸鱼鱼群岛写了封家书。

sentences.en: It was a letter to his wife and daughter, telling them not to worry, even if he was gone for many years.
sentences.zh: 这是写给妻子和女儿的信，告诉她们不要担心，即使他离开很多年也是如此。

sentences.en: Part of the plan was for the Franklin Expedition to spend multiple winters in the Arctic.
sentences.zh: 计划的一部分是让富兰克林远征队在北极度过多个冬天。

sentences.en: And the ship was provisioned to last that long.
sentences.zh: 船上的补给足够维持那么长时间。

sentences.en: As the Franklin Expedition left the coast of Greenland, one of Franklin's crew drew a pencil sketch of the Greenland Bay.
sentences.zh: 当富兰克林远征队离开格陵兰岛海岸时，富兰克林的一名船员画了一张格陵兰海湾的铅笔素描。

sentences.en: A lovely image of a single ship, floating alone, surrounded by ice and rock.
sentences.zh: 那是一幅可爱的画面：一艘孤零零的船漂浮着，四周环绕着冰山和岩石。

sentences.en: And with that, the crew began to sail up and over the very top of the globe.
sentences.zh: 就这样，船员们开始向北航行，驶向地球的最顶端。

sentences.en: Of course, Franklin and his crew were not actually the first explorers to make it this far into the Northwest Passage.
sentences.zh: 当然，富兰克林和他的船员并不是第一批深入西北航道的探险家。

sentences.en: And the idea that they could even discover it was wrong.
sentences.zh: 他们能够“发现”这条航道的想法本身就是错误的。

sentences.en: The Arctic waterways running from Greenland to Alaska had already been home to Arctic and Inuit peoples for over 4,000 years.
sentences.zh: 从格陵兰岛延伸到阿拉斯加的北极水道，4000多年来一直是北极和因纽特人的家园。

sentences.en: By the time Franklin came to find it, the Northwest Passage had been thoroughly explored by Inuit tribes,
sentences.zh: 在富兰克林来寻找它之前，西北航道已经被因纽特部落彻底探索过了，

sentences.en: as they hunted, fished, and settled across thousands of miles of Arctic coastline.
sentences.zh: 他们在数千英里的北极海岸线上狩猎、捕鱼和定居。

sentences.en: And as Franklin's expedition headed deeper and deeper into the Arctic, the Inuit watched from afar,
sentences.zh: 当富兰克林的探险队越走越深地进入北极时，因纽特人在远处注视着，

sentences.en: observing its progress through the passage and into the dangers that they already knew.
sentences.zh: 观察着它穿过航道并走向他们早已知道的危险之中。

sentences.en: Here on Beachy Island, at the upper reaches of the passage, are the graves of three ordinary sailors, doomed by extraordinary circumstances.
sentences.zh: 在航道最深处的比奇岛上，长眠着三名普通水手的坟墓，他们被非同寻常的环境判处了死刑。

sentences.en: During the first winter in the Arctic, the Franklin expedition hit an impasse,
sentences.zh: 在北极的第一个冬天，富兰克林探险队遇到了僵局，

sentences.en: a frozen expanse of ice that they couldn't sail through.
sentences.zh: 一片他们无法航行的冰冻冰原。

sentences.en: So they tried to turn around, but they were stuck.
sentences.zh: 于是他们试图掉头，但被困住了。

sentences.en: The way back had frozen solid.
sentences.zh: 回家的路已经冻得结结实实。

sentences.en: That in and of itself wasn't the end of the world.
sentences.zh: 这本身并不是世界末日。

sentences.en: It was full of ice, and they had expected something like this to happen.
sentences.zh: 这里到处都是冰，他们也预料到会发生类似的事情。

sentences.en: So they settled in for the first winter.
sentences.zh: 于是他们安顿下来过第一个冬天。

sentences.en: And during that winter, the first touch of death visited the expedition.
sentences.zh: 就在那个冬天，死神第一次造访了远征队。

sentences.en: Three men, 20-year-old John Torrington, 32-year-old William Brayne, and 25-year-old John Hartnell,
sentences.zh: 三个人：20岁的约翰·托灵顿、32岁的威廉·布雷恩和25岁的约翰·哈特内尔，

sentences.en: all died from some combination of pneumonia, malnourishment, zinc deficiency, and lead poisoning.
sentences.zh: 都死于肺炎、营养不良、锌缺乏和铅中毒的某种组合。

sentences.en: In fact, they may well have been ill when they first boarded the ship.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他们很可能在登船时就已经生病了。

sentences.en: When he died, 20-year-old John Torrington only weighed 85 pounds.
